title: AI reading of bank, check and brokerage records into structured evidence
problem: Forensic teams spend much of a project turning PDFs, scanned statements and check images into usable data; J.S. Held says this sometimes took as much as 50% of budgets.
approach: AI-enhanced text recognition turns bank, check and brokerage statements into reconciled data linked to the source documents; people then analyse it.
Every transaction is linked back to the original banking evidence before a report goes out; professionals interpret analyses and check flagged parties.
Full payor details for over 25,000 checks were ready in a few days rather than weeks, in one matter (self-reported).
Anders CPAs & Advisors principal says hand-keying is about 85% accurate and AI tools 99%, sometimes 100% (vendor-published).
who: J.S. Held, Valid8 Financial, Anders CPAs & Advisors

title: Matching every check and transaction to trace embezzlement and lapping
problem: Tracing a scheme across thousands of checks and accounts is slow by hand, and lapping (one customer's payments applied to another's account) is hard to see without matching every item.
approach: AI-assisted software matches every transaction and check to bank records, flags missing data and links each item back to evidence.
Forensic accountants interpret the matches, calculate losses and write the report; every item stays linked to the original evidence.
20,000 transactions across 10 accounts over five years were matched in hours; analysis that could take weeks took days (self-reported).
More than $7 million potentially embezzled in one matter and more than $30 million potentially misapplied payments in another (self-reported).

title: Continuous data monitoring and machine-learning anomaly detection in client anti-fraud programs
problem: Most occupational fraud is found by tips and runs for months before detection; analytics-based detection is in place in fewer than half of organisations in the ACFE study.
approach: Organisations and their advisers monitor transactions continuously and use machine learning to flag anomalies; investigators decide whether a flag is meaningful.
ACFE data measure monitoring in general, not AI: median loss $70,000 with it versus $150,000 without (independent).
Median duration was 9 months with monitoring versus 16 without; automated monitoring first detected 3% of cases, tips 43% (independent).
25% of surveyed organisations use AI or machine learning in anti-fraud programs, up from 18% in 2024 (vendor-published).
who: ACFE, SAS, CPA Practice Advisor, MDPI journal

title: Generative-AI first-pass document review in disputes and investigations
problem: First-level review of very large document sets is slow and costly, and results vary between human reviewers.
approach: A large language model applies the written review protocol to each document and returns a coding with rationale and citations.
Redgrave LLP case: aiR got 87.7% recall, 28.6% precision versus 64.4% and 39.2% for managed review (self-reported); researchers dispute comparability.
Relativity says aiR achieves 90%+ recall (vendor-published); Everlaw reports human-comparable results on four datasets (vendor-published).
People validate samples against an expert's coding and decisions stay with lawyers; first-level reviewers coded 34% of responsive documents non-responsive (independent).
who: Relativity, Everlaw, Redgrave LLP, Waterloo, Elevate

title: Plain-language questions over a live matter document set, with cited answers
problem: Early in a matter, teams need quick answers about people, events and key documents without waiting for a full review.
approach: Announced: Relativity's aiR Assist is a question-and-answer assistant running on matter data in the review platform, returning cited answers.
Practitioners verify answers against the cited source documents.
A customer quote on the vendor's page says it surfaces critical evidence in minutes (vendor-published).

title: Private-sandbox language model for document review in intellectual property damages disputes
problem: Patent-heavy disputes require reading a patent plus related patents, but time and cost limit how many related documents a team can review.
approach: J.S. Held's intellectual property practice says it is building models in a private sandbox so data is not disclosed to third parties.
The models are trained on industry data and prior work, then queried for document review, data requests and summaries.
A managing director reviews every item against original evidence, and analyses are double-checked with traditional methods.
The practice says AI greatly expands the related patents it can review; no figures published (self-reported).

title: Disclosure, verification and audit-trail rules for AI use in expert work
problem: Courts have excluded or discounted expert work when AI output was unverified or unexplainable, and counsel may now ask experts whether AI was used.
approach: Engagement letters add AI terms: written disclosure of tool, version and tasks, independent verification, closed-system tools only, and prompt and output logs.
J.S. Held's intellectual property practice amended its standard engagement letter to say it will use AI tools unless clients opt out.
The expert authors every opinion and can explain the method without the tool; counsel confirms AI use and verification before finalising.
Matter of Weber: re-running an expert's Copilot query gave three different results; Kohls v. Ellison: declaration excluded over non-existent citations (independent).
who: J.S. Held, Kilpatrick Townsend, US courts

title: AI red-flag screening of large document and email sets in fraud investigations
problem: Early-stage fraud work means sifting boxes of documents and thousands of emails for red flags.
approach: AI tools scan documents and emails for indicators; a forensic accountant assesses the candidates and explains results to courts and regulators.
Practitioners describe this; Diligent announced Smart Prep 360 for board materials, but no firm deployment with outcomes was found.
A BRG managing director says a review that took a summer by hand would take a few minutes with AI (self-reported).
Over 63% of surveyed forensic professionals reported better investigative processes from AI and data analytics (independent).

title: Generative-AI drafting of investigation and expert report outlines, narratives and charts
problem: Drafting reports, exhibits, transcript summaries and client emails takes expert time; Dean Dorton's deck asks how many monthly hours go on tasks AI could do in minutes.
approach: Generative AI produces a first outline or narrative, deposition summaries and draft charts, shown with Copilot in a Dean Dorton training deck.
The expert edits and owns the output and authors every opinion and conclusion.
The AICPA FVS 2026 conference has a scheduled session on AI in visualisation design.
Among the 16% of respondents using generative AI for anti-fraud, 45% use it for report writing (vendor-published).
who: Dean Dorton, AICPA & CIMA, SAS with ACFE

title: Preserving and collecting employees' generative-AI chats and prompts as evidence
problem: Employees' prompts and AI outputs may hold evidence, but they sit in tools that legal-hold and collection processes were not built for.
approach: Announced: Relativity says its platform can collect from Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack and more.
It says it can preserve in place, making enterprise AI chat data collectable alongside email and chat.
Counsel decides the scope of preservation and collection.

title: Idea: forensic examination of AI-generated or altered evidence such as deepfakes
problem: Idea, not a deployment: judges worry about hyperrealistic fake evidence, and fraudsters use AI to forge documents and impersonate people.
approach: Idea only: a forensic team would examine challenged items for provenance, access and alteration; no firm is found offering this.
Judges are advised to ask the source of a suspect item, who had access, whether it was altered, and for corroboration.
15 of 931 responding federal judges reported a deepfake challenge; 98% had not (independent).
77% of anti-fraud respondents report an increase in deepfake social engineering, and 75% in AI document forgery (vendor-published).

title: Idea: investigation services for AI-fuelled fraud and AI-washing claims
problem: Idea, not a deployment: clients expect more AI-enabled fraud and claims overstating a company's AI capabilities ('AI washing'), and few feel prepared.
approach: Idea only: forensic accountants would investigate AI-enabled schemes and test AI claims; no firm reports delivering this.
Investigators would decide scope, interview and report findings.
Only 7% of respondents say their organisations are more than moderately prepared for AI-fuelled fraud (vendor-published).
In March 2024 the SEC settled charges against two investment advisers over misleading statements about AI use; $400,000 total penalties (independent).

title: Idea: agentic AI for blockchain and cryptocurrency fund tracing
problem: Idea, not a deployment: following funds through intermediary wallets to exchanges and mixers is manual and requires specialised tooling.
approach: Idea only: a scheduled AICPA FVS session on blockchain tracing says it will discuss agentic AI; no deployment or product is described.
Attendees are trained to follow on-chain flows themselves.

title: Idea: AI critique of opposing expert reports and cross-examination preparation
problem: Idea, not a deployment: experts and counsel must find flaws in opposing analyses and prepare for cross-examination under time pressure.
approach: Idea: a language model summarises an opposing expert's report, lists probing questions or flags inconsistencies; no outcomes published.
J.S. Held says attorneys use AI during depositions and trials this way; a Dean Dorton deck demonstrates a mock critique with Copilot.
The expert reviews the output and keeps independent judgment.

title: Idea: error-rate validation studies of machine analyses under proposed Rule 707
problem: Idea, not a deployment: if machine output is offered without an expert, the proponent would have to show it meets Rule 702's reliability tests.
approach: Idea only: experts would design and run validation studies (training data, error rates, independent replication) or test an opponent's tool.
The draft committee note says a proponent may overcome inexplicability by showing how the machine was trained and a low error rate.
Rule 707 is a proposal and may change; the court decides admissibility.
